source:
Make a simple 3D endless runner. Keep it simple - do NOT do prompt
enhancement or a big requirements write-up, and don't expand the scope. I
just want one small, polished, ~5-minute playable game, nothing more.

- Fully 3D (render a real WebGL scene). Works on mobile, touch and mouse,
 in both portrait and landscape.
- Third-person camera behind and slightly above the runner, looking down
 the track.
- The runner auto-runs forward; tap/swipe left-right to switch lanes,
 tap/swipe up to jump. Dodge obstacles and grab coins. Speed increases
 slowly over time.
- Crashing into an obstacle ends the run - show the run distance and coins
 with a Retry button.
- Save the player's best distance on the server and show it in the HUD.

That's the whole game. No shops, no extra modes, no upgrade systems - just
the core run loop, made to feel good.

answers.ask: No setting was given - should the track read as city, desert, neon, or deliberately abstract?
answers.answer: Use a deliberately abstract, clean arcade runner look so the core movement and obstacles stay readable.

answers.ask: The track is endless, so only a chunk can be framed - is a few-hundred-stud segment the right unit to draw?
answers.answer: Yes, use a few-hundred-stud visible/recycled track segment; that is enough for this small endless runner.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No setting was given - should the track read as city, desert, neon, or deliberately abstract? A: Use a deliberately abstract, clean arcade runner look so the core movement and obstacles stay readable.
- [author] scale — Q: The track is endless, so only a chunk can be framed - is a few-hundred-stud segment the right unit to draw? A: Yes, use a few-hundred-stud visible/recycled track segment; that is enough for this small endless runner.
- [agent_inferred] lane count — Q: How many fixed lanes should left-right inputs switch between? A: Use three fixed lanes, the narrow standard arrangement that supports both left and right switching.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a clean abstract 3D endless-runner track shown as one polished, few-hundred-stud visible segment. Run three fixed parallel lanes away from the lower foreground toward the horizon, with simple readable jump obstacles and lane-blocking hazards distributed along the route. Keep the modular track straight and seamless so additional segments can recycle beyond view. Leave clear reaction space between obstacles as speed increases, and omit shops, side modes, upgrades, scenery themes, and any terminal finish.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Infinite Runner: forward motion is automatic, the path is endless, and the player reacts by switching lanes and jumping.

## Shape and preset
Use `lane-snap`, named Fixed Lane Snap: movement snaps between exactly three rigid lanes. The preset is Lane Runner, retaining deterministic chunks and coin trails while replacing its moving-obstacle assumption with the simple jump and collision obstacles the author requested.

## Config requirements
Use `chunk-modular` for straight modular segments whose origins and exits align exactly. Use `obstacle-jump` for readable barriers and gaps across selected lanes. Use `hazard-kill` for solid lane obstacles that end the run on contact. Use the visible side of `spawn-area` for the clear initial runner position at the rear of the first chunk.

## Layout requirements
Use `collectible-nodes` for coin trails laid along lanes, including occasional lane changes without blocking every safe route. Use `trigger-despawn` at the rear edge of the recycled segment, safely behind the camera. Place one `spawn-area` marker in the center lane of the initial chunk. Obstacle spacing remains elastic at roughly current speed times 0.5 seconds of reaction time.

## Layout components
One visible queue of modular track chunks forms three straight lanes across a few hundred studs. Obstacles occupy selected lane intervals; coins trace safe or riskier lines between them. The rear start and cleanup edge sit behind the camera-facing foreground, while the open forward edge aligns with the next chunk. No finish zone exists.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: validate lane widths, modular pivots, clearable obstacle spacing, and coin routes before dressing the track.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium because the visible recycled unit is a few hundred studs while individual obstacles and coins must remain readable. The theme is clean abstract arcade geometry. Use `P6` because chunks, lanes, and speed-dependent obstacle sequences must be valid by construction.
